Consider the ellipse centered at $(-3,4)$ with horizontal radius $2$ and vertical radius $6,$ as shown above. Construct a set of parametric equations, defined for $\theta \in [0,2\pi ),$ that traverse the ellipse once in the counterclockwise direction starting at the point $A(-1,4).$

question.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of an ellipse centered at the point $(h,k)$ with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ are

$$
x=a\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +h,\,y=b\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +k,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

Under this parametrization, the ellipse is traversed once in the counterclockwise direction, starting from $(h+a,k).$

In our case, the ellipse is centered at the point $(-3,4),$ $a=2$ and $b=6.$ Therefore, the parametric equations of the ellipse are 

$$
x=2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta -3,\,y=6\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta +4,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$
